attributes.name: host_description
attributes.value: Patient with active polysubstance use disorder presents with fever and joint pain after leaving outside hospital two weeks prior against medical advice following diagnosis of infective endocarditis. Blood cultures positive for methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus. Transesophageal echocardiogram visualizes extensive tricuspid valve vegetations. Patient underwent tricuspid valve repair surgery with porcine valve replacement and dual-lead pacemaker placement. Course complicated by septic pulmonary emboli with multiple cavitary lesions. Managed medically with vancomycin plus ceftaroline transitioned to daptomycin monotherapy (10 mg/kg) upon discharge to rehab facility. Duration of bacteremia: 3 days.

description.comment: aliases: B0623, R11077. Other isolates from the same patient: BSN53-2

attributes.name: host_description
attributes.value: Patient presents with a mechanical fall secondary to impulsive behavior at outside skilled nursing facility. Past medical history is significant for stroke-related dementia, seizure disorder and metastatic lung cancer. Patient course complicated by a lacunar infarct, staphylococcal pneumonia with bacteremia and septic vs. oncologic spinal metastases. Medical management included cefepime, azithromycin and vancomycin, consolidated to daptomycin plus doxycycline on discharge. Discharged in stable condition to long-term acute care center for further management. Duration of bacteremia: 1 day.

attributes.name: host_description
attributes.value: Patient with end-stage renal disease presents from home with shortness of breath and hypotension. Patient was treated for central line-associated bacterial bloodstream infection (methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus) with vancomycin plus cefazolin. Clinical course was complicated by troponinemia, bilateral pulmonary emboli and persistent hypotension. Patient remained persistently hypotensive requiring multiple fluid boluses. Patient became asystolic and return of spontaneous circulation could not be established. Duration of bacteremia: 2 days.

attributes.name: host_description
attributes.value: Patient with history of spinal osteomyelitis and septic arthritis presents with lower back pain following completion of daptomycin therapy for prior infection. Magnetic resonance imaging revealed a lumbar spinal abscess. Transesophageal echocardiogram imaging was unremarkable. Patient was managed surgically with incision and drainage and hemilaminectomy. Medical management included vancomycin with cefazolin transitioned to daptomycin consolidated to linezolid on discharge to skilled nursing facility with planned transition to doxycycline suppressive therapy. Duration of bacteremia: 4 days.

attributes.name: host_description
attributes.value: Patient with history of peripheral vascular disease and uncontrolled diabetes presents with polymicrobial, non-healing left lower extremity wound extending to exposed bone. Clinical course was complicated by polymicrobial bacteremia including Proteus mirabilis and Staphylococcus aureus. Surgical management included below-the-knee amputation. Medical management included vancomycin plus cefepime transitioned to daptomycin, cefepime and metronidazole. Patient was stabilized and left against medical advice prior to rehabilitation placement. Duration of bacteremia: 8 days.

attributes.value: Patient with end-stage renal disease presents with lower back pain and staphylococcal bacteremia secondary to an infected catheter. Magnetic resonance imaging reveales lumbosacral osteomyelitis with epidural phlegmon, abscess and localized arachnoiditis. Surgical management included laminectomy and epidural phlegmon evacuation. Medical management included vancomycin transitioned to daptomycin. Patient was discharged in stable condition to a skilled nursing facility. Duration of bacteremia: 6 days.

attributes.name: host_description
attributes.value: Patient with COPD, heart failure and end-stage renal disease presents with shortness of breath. Treated with emergent dialysis for fluid overload with incidental finding of staphylococcal bacteremia. Echocardiogram and MRI unremarkable. Chest X-ray revealed bibasalar pneumonia. Initial treatment with vancomycin plus cefepime consolidated to ceftaroline monotherapy, then broadened to daptomycin plus linezolid and piperacillin-tazobactam. Discharged to subacute rehab facility with daptomycin monotherapy for total of 4 weeks. Duration of bacteremia: 8 days.

attributes.name: host_description
attributes.value: Patient presented with shortness of breath and hemoptysis secondary to multifocal staphylococcal pneumonia. Patient clinical course was complicated by concomitant staphylococcal bacteremia, acute hypoxic respiratory failure requiring intubation and empyema. Computed tomography revealed multiple loculations consistent with pleural abscesses and left lobular nodules consistent with septic pulmonary emboli. Patient demonstrated significant functional improvement following abscess drainage and video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery was not pursued. Patient was managed medically with vancomycin monotherapy advanced to daptomycin plus ceftaroline and consolidated back to vancomycin monotherapy prior to discharge in stable condition to a skilled nursing facility. Duration of bacteremia: 5 days.

attributes.name: host_description
attributes.value: Patient with history of spinal osteomyelitis and recent staphylococcal bacteremia presents with back pain. Patient was managed surgically with planned cervicothoracic laminectomy and fusion. Patient presented on daptomycin therapy related to her previous encounter which was held prior to surgery. Post-surgical blood cultures were positive for Staphylococcus aureus and daptomycin therapy resumed. Patient was stabilized and discharged back to skilled nursing facility. Duration of bacteremia: 3 days.

attributes.name: host_description
attributes.value: Patient with history of paraplegia, osteomyelitis, sacral ulcers and chronic deep vein thromboses presents with left hip pain. Workup revealed left hip abscess, chronic osteomyelitis and polymicrobial bacteremia including Streptococcus dysgalactiae, Enterococcus faecalis and Staphylococcus aureus. Clinical course was complicated by septic shock, acute anemia and osteonecrosis. Patient was managed medically with vancomycin, cefepime and metronidazole with cefepime and ampicillin-sulbactam to prescribed on discharge. Patient refused surgical interventions and was discharged home in stable condition. Duration of bacteremia: 3 days.

attributes.value: Patient presents on transfer from outside hospital for advanced imaging in the setting of persistent staphylococcal bacteremia of unknown source. At outside hospital, magnetic resonance imaging, transthoracic echocardiogram and tagged white blood cell scan were all unremarkable despite persistent culture positivity in the context of appropriate vancomycin and daptomycin therapy. During current encounter, transesophageal echocardiogram and computed tomography were both unremarkable. Patient was managed medically with ceftaroline and discharged in stable condition to subacute rehabilitation facility. Duration of bacteremia, including stay at outside hospital: 22 days.

attributes.name: host_description
attributes.value: Patient with recent cervical fracture, status-post laminectomy and tracheostomy, presented from subacute rehabilitation for evaluation of septic shock. Workup revealed acute respiratory failure secondary to staphylococcal bacteremia with new sacral ulceration as presumed source. Clinical course was complicated by a cervical spine hematoma extending into the interspinous space, ligamentum flavum disruption secondary to same, superventricular tachycardia refractory to cardioversion, acute kidney injury with acute tubular necrosis in the context of active urosepsis, severe protein calorie malnutrition and acute-on-chronic anemia secondary to hematuria. Patient was managed medically with cefazolin to be continued on discharge. Patient was a poor candidate for spinal surgery and could not receive transesophageal echocardial imaging due to spinal injury. Patient was stabilized and discharged to subacute rehabilitation facility. Duration of bacteremia: 4 days.

attributes.name: host_description
attributes.value: Patient with history of staphylococcal osteomyelitis and active substance use disorder presents with acute neck pain at his heroin injection site. Patient was observed to be bacteremic and treated medically with vancomycin plus cefazolin. Clinical course was complicated by extensive spinal osteomyelitis and paraspinal abscesses, multiple pulmonary opacities consistent with septic emboli and tricuspid valve endocarditis. Blood cultures consistently grew out two populations of Staphylococcus aureus, one methicillin-resistant and one methicillin-susceptible. Therapy was modified to daptomycin plus cefazolin resulting in pure methicillin-resistant cultures then clear blood cultures. The patient experienced relapse bacteremia two weeks later with daptomycin nonsusceptible methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus and therapy was modified again to ceftaroline plus daptomycin. The following week the patient left against medical advice and was prescribed oral linezolid to complete therapy. Duration of initial bacteremia: 14 days.

attributes.value: Patient presents with status epilepticus secondary to medication nonadherence. Transesophageal echocardiogram was unremarkable and patient was managed medically with cefazolin. attributes.value: Patient presents as a John Doe found down by emergency medical services. Presentation included large sinus and posterior neck abscesses extending to the spine, leukocytosis, hypertensive crisis, extensor posturing and a urine drug screen positive for amphetamine and cocaine. Clinical course was complicated by intubation and pressor support dependencies, unilateral ocular hypertension requiring canthotomy, staphylococcal bacteremia treated with meropenem and persistent hypovolemia refractory to fluid bolus resulting in hypovolemic hyponatremia. Computed tomography of the head revealed a cerebral sinus venous thrombosis. Neurological exam declined with brain stem reflexes and brain blood flow absent indicative of brain death. Duration of bacteremia: 3 days

attributes.name: host_description
attributes.value: Patient with history of ventilator-dependent respiratory failure secondary to COVID-19 pneumonia and multiple ischemic cerebrovascular accidents presents from extended care facility with acute mental status changes. Patient was diagnosed with polymicrobial bacteremia including methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus and multiple gram-negative organisms managed with daptomycin plus cefepime transitioned to vancomycin, ceftriaxone and minocycline on discharge. Clinical course was complicated by a large necrotic sacral decubitus ulcer extending to the bone as a presumed bacteremia source, mucus plugging versus atelactasis resulting in hypoxia, non-ST segement elevation myocardial infarction resulting in pulseless electrical activity requiring two rounds of cardiopulmonary resuscitation and epinepherine before return of spontaneous circulation, anemia requiring multiple transfusions and severe peripheral vasoocclusive disease. Patient was denied placement at a long term acute care facility and discharged to a skilled nursing facility. Duration of staphylococcal bacteremia: 6 days.

Clinical course was complicated by COVID-19 positivity, cardiac arrest, acute hypoxemic respiratory failure secondary to pulmonary emboli, mitral valve infective endocarditis and inflammation at the hemodialysis access site. attributes.value: Clinical bloodstream isolate CUBIST-33 is part of the Cubist Pharmaceuticals Isolate Collection. CUBIST-33 is the daptomycin-resistant isolate of the CUBIST-32/CUBIST-33 sequential isolate paired strains obtained from a patient with endovascular staphylococcal infection following daptomycin treatment failure. It is multilocus sequence type 5, clonal complex 5, SCCmec-IVa (+), spa type t002 / T1-J1-M1-B1-M1-D1-M1-G1-M1-K1. Compared to CUBIST-32, CUBIST-33 has sequence variations in walK (L494V), and in mprF (S337L). It was previously described in a 2015 report as strain "C33".

The annotation was added by the NCBI Prokaryotic Genome Annotation Pipeline (PGAP). Information about PGAP can be found here: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/genome/annotation_prok/
The genome was annotated via NCBI's Prokaryotic Genomes Automatic Annotation Pipeline, followed by manual curation. Information about the Pipeline can be found here: http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/genomes/static/Pipeline.html. Please be aware that the annotation is done automatically with little or no manual curation.
